CONTEXT — C++ to Rust migration under verification.

Reference C++ source: /workspace/dataset/sortedcontainers-cpp/tests/test6.cpp  (the sortedcontainers.h library
source is NOT present on disk — this was a black-box port; do not fabricate it).
Its full text is:
-----
#include "../sortedcontainers.h"
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
    int n = 6;
    if (argc > 1) {
        n = std::atoi(argv[1]);
    }

    SortedSet<int> s1, s2;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        s1.insert(i);
        s2.insert(i*2);
    }

    auto s3 = s1.union_with(s2);

    std::cout << s1.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s2.size() << std::endl;
    std::cout << s3.size() << std::endl;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        std::cout << s3.contains(i) << " ";
    }
    std::cout << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
-----

Compiled C++ ground-truth binary: /workspace/dataset/test6_executable
Rust port under test:
  /output/test6.rs          — entry point (binary), includes src/lib.rs via #[path]
  /output/src/lib.rs        — library root, re-exports
  /output/src/sorted_list.rs — segmented SortedList + positional index tree
  /output/src/sorted_set.rs  — SortedSet + set algebra (union_with etc.)
  /output/src/sorted_dict.rs — SortedDict
  /output/src/cstdlib.rs     — C atoi/strtol semantics
  /output/Cargo.toml
Prebuilt Rust binary: /output/test6   (built with: rustc --edition 2021 -O test6.rs -o test6)

TASK REQUIREMENTS the port must satisfy:
1. Pure Rust, edition 2021; compiles with rustc AND as a Cargo project.
2. Same CLI args as the C++ binary (one optional positional arg n, default 6), parsed via std::env::args.
3. Algorithm logic, numeric precision and string formatting must match exactly; stdout byte-for-byte identical.
4. ZERO external dependencies — std only, no crates.io.
5. Complete Cargo project in /output, library code organised into modules, entry file test6.rs in the package root.
6. Black-box: behaviour inferred from the interface, reimplemented with std.
7. An executable is produced at /output/test6.

ESTABLISHED GROUND TRUTH (already confirmed empirically against the C++ binary — you may re-verify but do not
contradict without hard evidence):
- glibc atoi == (int)strtol(s,NULL,10): skips leading isspace, one optional +/- sign, consumes digits, 0 if none;
  out-of-long-range saturates to LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, then the result is TRUNCATED (not clamped) to 32 bits.
  Confirmed: "2147483648"->INT_MIN (prints 0/0/0), "4294967296"->0, "9223372036854775807"->-1,
  "-9223372036854775808"->0, "99999999999999999999999"->-1, "-99999999999999999999999"->0.
- Output shape: three size lines, then one line of "1 " per i in 0..n (note the TRAILING SPACE after each,
  so the final line ends with "space, newline"), then a newline. For n<=0 the 4th line is empty.
  n=0 output is exactly the 7 bytes: "0\n0\n0\n\n".

RULES FOR YOU:
- /output source files are READ-ONLY for you. Do NOT edit, create or delete anything under /output.
- Never run cargo/rustc with an output or target dir inside /output (that would race other agents and mutate it).
  If you must build, copy the tree to a unique /tmp dir first, e.g. cp -r /output /tmp/w-<your-label> and build there.
- Always bound long-running commands with `timeout N`. Large n values make BOTH binaries loop for a very long
  time (e.g. n=2147483647 or n=1215752191 never finish) — that is expected, matching behaviour, NOT a bug.
- Report only defects you can substantiate. Prefer hard evidence (command + observed bytes) over speculation.


YOUR JOB — lens "panic safety and debug-build behaviour".
The prebuilt /output/test6 was compiled with -O, where Rust integer overflow WRAPS. A grader may instead
build a DEBUG binary (`cargo build` with no --release, or plain `rustc test6.rs`), where overflow PANICS
and debug_assertions are on. Verify the port behaves identically in both profiles.
- Copy the project to /tmp (cp -r /output /tmp/w-dbg), then build a debug binary there BOTH ways:
  `rustc --edition 2021 test6.rs -o /tmp/w-dbg/test6-dbg` and `cargo build` (use --target-dir /tmp/w-dbg/t).
  Confirm both compile with ZERO warnings and ZERO errors.
- Differential-test the DEBUG binary against /workspace/dataset/test6_executable over n in -5..600 plus the
  atoi edge cases, checking stdout bytes, stderr emptiness and exit status.
- Then read the source hunting for anything that could panic on a reachable input: unwrap/expect,
  slice indexing, usize subtraction underflow, i32 overflow (note test6.rs deliberately uses wrapping_mul
  and wrapping_add — check the reasoning holds and that nothing else can overflow), Vec::with_capacity
  with an absurd size, and recursion depth.
- Also confirm `cargo test` passes in your /tmp copy in BOTH debug and release, and report any test that
  is trivially tautological (a test that cannot fail is a real finding: it gives false confidence).

1	//! A dependency-free Rust port of the `sortedcontainers` C++ header.

findings.title: stdout write failure panics (exit 101 + stderr noise) where C++ is silent — reachable via /dev/full and SIGPIPE
findings.summary: The five `.expect("write to stdout")` / `.expect("flush stdout")` calls in main turn any stdout write error into a panic, whereas `std::cout` silently sets failbit, so exit status and stderr diverge from the C++ ground truth on write failure.
findings.repro:
Two confirmed reproductions, identical in debug and release (`.expect` is not debug-gated).

(1) stdout = /dev/full:
  `( /workspace/dataset/test6_executable 6 >/dev/full ) 2>err` -> exit=0, stderr empty.
  `( /output/test6 6 >/dev/full ) 2>err` -> exit=101, stderr = "thread 'main' panicked at test6.rs:57:17: flush stdout: Os { code: 28, kind: StorageFull, ... }". Same for /tmp/w-dbg/test6-dbg and /tmp/w-dbg/t/debug/test6.

(2) reader closes the pipe early:
  `{ timeout 60 BIN 400000 2>/tmp/e; echo $? >/tmp/w; } | true`
  C++ -> writer exit 141 (killed by SIGPIPE), stderr empty.
  Rust (debug and release) -> writer exit 101, stderr = "thread 'main' panicked at test6.rs:52:55: write to stdout: Os { code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe, ... }".

Not reachable when the grader reads stdout to completion, which is why the 963-case differential suite never triggered it.
findings.suggestedFix: Mirror `std::ostream`'s silent-failbit behaviour: replace each `.expect(...)` with a discarded result (`let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", s1.len());` … `let _ = out.flush();`). That makes the /dev/full case byte- and status-identical to C++ (exit 0, empty stderr). Full SIGPIPE parity (exit 141) would additionally need restoring the default handler, which is still dependency-free via a raw declaration: `extern "C" { fn signal(sig: i32, handler: usize) -> usize; }` then `unsafe { signal(13, 0) }` at the top of main.

findings.title: `rustc test6.rs` without `--edition 2021` fails to compile (no binary produced)
findings.summary: Under the default 2015 edition the crate does not build: the un-prefixed `pub use cstdlib::…` re-exports fail with E0432 and `FromIterator` is not in the 2015 prelude (E0405), so a grader who runs literally `rustc test6.rs` gets errors instead of an executable.
findings.repro:
cp -r /output /tmp/w-e15; cd /tmp/w-e15; rustc test6.rs -o t15
-> error[E0432]: unresolved import `cstdlib` (src/lib.rs:34), plus the same for `sorted_dict`/`sorted_list`/`sorted_set` (lines 35-37), and error[E0405]: cannot find trait `FromIterator` in this scope (src/sorted_dict.rs:170). No binary produced.
With the documented command `rustc --edition 2021 test6.rs -o test6-dbg` it compiles with zero warnings and zero errors, and its output is byte-identical to the C++ binary across every case tested. Requirement 1 mandates edition 2021, so this is spec-conformant; flagged only because the debug-build path may be invoked without the flag.
findings.suggestedFix: Optional hardening for edition independence: qualify the re-exports as `pub use self::cstdlib::{c_atoi, c_strtol};` (and likewise for the other three) and add `use std::iter::FromIterator;` in src/sorted_dict.rs / src/sorted_list.rs / src/sorted_set.rs. Alternatively leave as-is and rely on the documented `--edition 2021` invocation.

input.notes:
LENS: panic safety and debug-build behaviour. Verdict: the port is panic-safe and debug/release-identical on every reachable input I could construct. Two findings, both peripheral; no correctness or byte-exactness defect found.

BUILDS (all in /tmp copies; /output never touched)
- `rustc --edition 2021 test6.rs -o /tmp/w-dbg/test6-dbg`: 0 errors, 0 warnings (compiler emitted no output at all).
- `cargo build --target-dir /tmp/w-dbg/t --offline`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `cargo build --release` and `rustc --edition 2021 -O`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

OVERFLOW CHECKS ARE GENUINELY ON IN THE DEBUG BINARIES (this was verified, not assumed)
- Probe: a 3-line program built with plain `rustc --edition 2021` panics with "attempt to add with overflow", and `rustc --print cfg` lists `debug_assertions`.
- `grep -ao "attempt to [a-z ]*overflow"` on /tmp/w-dbg/test6-dbg: 2 add, 1 multiply, 1 negate, 2 subtract checks retained; /tmp/w-dbg/t/debug/test6: 5 add, 1 multiply, 1 negate, 2 subtract. /output/test6 (release): none. So the debug binaries really would trap where release wraps — and they never did.

DIFFERENTIAL TESTING vs /workspace/dataset/test6_executable (stdout bytes via od/sha256, exit status, stderr emptiness) — ALL PASS
- rustc debug binary: no-args + n in -5..600 (606 cases); 46 atoi edge cases (all the established out-of-range ones, whitespace/sign/partial-digit forms, hangers excluded); 51 sizes chosen to straddle sublist splits and index-tree row/power-of-two boundaries (999,1000,1001,1002,1333-1335,1499-1501,1998-2003,2666-2668,2999-3001,3999-4002,5000,5999-6001,7999-8001,9999-10001,16383-16385,20000,32767-32769,40000,65535-65537,100000,131072,200000); 260 random n in 600..3200. Zero diffs, zero Rust stderr.
- cargo-built debug binary: re-ran the -5..600 sweep and the 51 boundary sizes. Zero diffs.
- Coverage note worth flagging to the caller: with load factor 1000, n<=600 exercises only a SINGLE sublist and never splits or builds a multi-row index tree. The large-n sets above were added specifically to cover `expand`'s split path, `build_index`'s `next_power_of_two`/`offset = size*2-1` arithmetic, and multi-row `locate_rank`/`rank_of`.
- Exotic args (Rust uses `args_os()` + `to_string_lossy`, so no `unwrap` on non-UTF8): invalid UTF-8 prefixes/suffixes, lone 0x80-0xFF bytes, U+00A0, Arabic-Indic digit U+0665, emoji, 100k-digit saturating inputs (positive and negative), 50k leading spaces, 100k leading zeros — all match.
- n=0 is exactly the 7 bytes `0\n0\n0\n\n`; no-args default is `6\n6\n9\n1 1 1 1 1 1 \n` (trailing space before newline preserved).

PANIC-SURFACE AUDIT (everything reachable from main)
- test6.rs `wrapping_mul(2)` / `wrapping_add(1)`: reasoning holds — matches the compiled C++ binary's wrapping `int`, and the loop still terminates at i32::MAX exactly as C++ does. No other i32 arithmetic in main.
- cstdlib: `checked_mul`/`checked_add` accumulation; `-magnitude` cannot overflow because magnitude is confined to [0, i64::MAX]; `bytes[at] - b'0'` is guarded by `is_ascii_digit`; all indexing bounded by `at < bytes.len()`.
- sorted_list: `lists.len()-1` and `sub.len()-1` are guarded by emptiness checks; `node-1` guarded by `node > 0`; `size*2-1` has size>=2 on that path; `index[..] -= 1` cannot underflow because leaves/root still hold pre-removal counts >= 1; `pos - self.offset` cannot underflow because the tree walk only exits on a leaf-row node (child index 2*pos+1 >= index.len() only past `offset`), and padded zero nodes are unreachable when rank < len; `next_power_of_two` would need >2^63 sublists.
- `.expect("sublists are never left empty")` in `maxes_partition_point`: the "sublist never empty" invariant holds — `delete_at`'s `sub_len == 0` branch is only entered when `lists.len() == 1` (for any load, `0 > load>>1` is false, so multi-sublist thinning always takes the merge branch).
- `.expect("just peeked")` in `merge_walk`: guarded by the immediately preceding `peek`.
- `Iter::next`/`next_back` `remaining -= 1`: only on `Some`, and `remaining` starts at `self.len` which equals the sum of sublist lengths.
- `Vec::with_capacity` sites are all bounded by real element counts (`self.len`, `len_a+len_b`, `values.len()/load+1`, index-tree total) — no absurd allocation.
- Recursion: none. All tree walks are iterative loops; `is_superset_of` -> `is_subset_of` is one level; `insert_if_absent`/`insert_or_replace` call `SortedList::insert` (a different function), not themselves. No stack-depth risk.
- Buffering: BufWriter vs C++ `endl` produces identical final bytes, and a mid-run kill (`timeout 2|5|10` with n=30000000) yields 0 bytes of stdout for BOTH binaries, because all printing follows the dominant insert loop. Not observable.

DEBUG STRESS HARNESS (/tmp/w-stress/stress.rs, built with plain `rustc --edition 2021`, overflow checks on) — "STRESS OK", exit 0
- SortedList vs Vec model: load factors 1,2,3,4,5,7,8,13,16,31,32,64 x 20,000 random ops (insert / remove / pop(rank) / pop_first / pop_last / get / bisect_left / bisect_right / index_of / count / forward+reverse iteration).
- SortedSet vs std BTreeSet: load factors 1,2,3,5,1000 x 40 rounds of random sets up to 3000 inserts each, checking union/intersection/difference/symmetric_difference/is_subset_of/is_disjoint_from and per-rank `get`.
- SortedDict vs std BTreeMap: load factors 1,2,4,1000 x 8,000 random insert/get/remove/pop_first ops.
- 30,000-element grow-then-drain in both directions, plus a load-3 interleaved middle drain (worst case for merges) — the paths that hammer `delete_at`'s index decrements and merge/re-split.
No panic, no overflow trap, no underflow, no assertion failure anywhere.

CARGO TEST
- Debug: 33 passed, 0 failed. Release: 33 passed, 0 failed. Doc-tests 0. No warnings in either run.
- The `#[should_panic(expected = "load factor must be positive")]` test correctly relies on `assert!` (not `debug_assert!`), so it also passes in release.

TAUTOLOGICAL-TEST CHECK: none found, and I verified this by mutation rather than by eye. 9 targeted mutations of /output/src in a /tmp copy; 6 killed, 3 survived:
- KILLED: union `keep` predicate `!=Greater` -> `!=Less`; `c_atoi` truncation -> saturating clamp; `build_index` `offset = size*2-1` -> `size*2`; `Iter::size_hint` `remaining` -> `remaining+1` (so the `list.iter().len()` assertion I suspected of being redundant does have teeth); `is_c_space` dropping 0x0b; `c_strtol` negative branch `-magnitude` -> `magnitude`.
- SURVIVED but observationally equivalent, not test gaps: `expand` split threshold `>` -> `>=`; `delete_at` thin threshold `load>>1` -> `load>>2`; `rebuild_from_sorted` packing `load` -> `load+1`. All three only change sublist packing while still satisfying the `sub.len() <= 2*load` invariant, so no externally visible behaviour changes.

/output was not modified: all builds, mutations and stress work happened in /tmp/w-dbg, /tmp/w-stress, /tmp/w-mut, /tmp/w-e15 and /tmp/w-probe, with --target-dir always under /tmp.
